Q: How to determine version of openssl library? A:

You can do this programatically by reading the following:

  • OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER(3)

and

  • SSLeay_version(3)

Basically, you will need to use the following functions:

  • SSLeay()

  • SSLeay_version()

OpenSSL 3.0 Update

OpenSSL 3.0 introduces OpenSSL_version() and OPENSSL_info() to replace the above.

Q: How to stop Google sheet from auto convert dates to numbers? A:

I don't think its possible to change the automatic behavior, however, based in the official documentation as a workaround you can use the API to send a batch update to change the cell format to Date.

For this you would need to use the API method spreadsheets.batchUpdate and include a UpdateCells request. What you are looking to modify in the request is the NumberFormatType parameter and set the value to DATE in order to change the format.

References:

  • Method: spreadsheets.batchUpdate
  • UpdateCells
  • NumberFormatType

Q: How do I start two activities at same time? A:

There are 2 ways to do what you want:

  1. The first way is to launch one of the activities (the one you want "in the background") and have that Activity launch the other one (the one you want "in the foreground") immediately (in onCreate(). When the top Activity is finished, the other one (the "background" Activity) will be shown.

  2. The second way to do this is to simply launch the Activity that you want to be in the "foreground". In this Activity you can override onBackPressed() to launch the other ("background") Activity. In this way, the user experience is as you desire, but you don't need to launch the "background" Activity until it needs to be shown to the user. Depending on your requirements, you can also switch back and forth between these 2 activities, by simply calling startActivity() with an Intent where you have set Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_REORDER_TO_FRONT when you want to move from one Activity to another. In this case, Android will bring an existing instance of the target Activity to the front of the task (if it exists) or will launch a new instance of the target Activity (if one does not already exist).

However, none of your terminology is correct and that causes problems when communicating with other developers. An Activity isn't in the "foreground" or the "background". These terms are used when talking about tasks. A task is in the "foreground" when the user is interacting with it and it is shown on screen. Other tasks are in the "background". A task is made up of one (or more) activities, and they are stacked in such a way that the top-most Activity is the one that the user is interacting with. The other activities in the task are not "in the background", they are just paused.
